# Phase 6A: log-OLS versus Poisson QMLE gravity

**Generated by** `scripts/phase6a_compare.py`. Both estimators scored on the
**same** 20% holdout (`gravity.holdout_split`, seed 7) from the same market
frame, so the comparison is like for like.

**Baseline** `docs/W1.4_baseline_freeze.md`, commit `bd7d4dd`.

All calibration is binned by **predicted** value. Binning by observed value
conditions on the outcome and manufactures a monotonic pattern from noise; that
error is what the A5 correction was about.

---

## 1. Headline metrics

### Vintage `current` (2023-2024), holdout n = 1,214

| metric | log_ols | poisson_qmle | better |
|---|---|---|---|
| **aggregate pred / obs** | 0.4352 | **0.9481** | Poisson |
| MAPE | **1.050** | 1.849 | OLS |
| median APE | **0.6153** | 0.7402 | OLS |
| RMSE | 233,700 | **168,100** | Poisson, 28% lower |
| RMSLE | **1.001** | 1.128 | OLS |

### Vintage `pre2022` (2018-2019), holdout n = 1,205

| metric | log_ols | poisson_qmle | better |
|---|---|---|---|
| **aggregate pred / obs** | 0.4508 | **1.046** | Poisson |
| MAPE | **0.8678** | 1.487 | OLS |
| median APE | **0.5995** | 0.7221 | OLS |
| RMSE | 198,700 | **153,600** | Poisson, 23% lower |
| RMSLE | **0.968** | 1.088 | OLS |

**This is a trade, not a clean win, and the direction is exactly what theory
predicts.** MAPE, median APE and RMSLE are relative-error measures dominated by
the many small markets, and they reward an estimator that targets the
conditional median. Aggregate ratio and RMSE are level measures dominated by the
few large markets, and they reward an estimator that targets the conditional
mean. OLS targets the median; Poisson targets the mean. Each wins the metrics
aligned with its own objective.

The question is which objective a route-planning system needs. See section 6.

## 2. Log residual distribution, ln(obs) - ln(pred)

| vintage | estimator | mean | median | sd | skew |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| current | log_ols | -0.0319 | -0.1150 | 1.0014 | 0.427 |
| current | poisson_qmle | -0.3938 | -0.4613 | 1.0573 | 0.369 |
| pre2022 | log_ols | 0.0421 | -0.0945 | 0.9674 | 0.720 |
| pre2022 | poisson_qmle | -0.2977 | -0.4082 | 1.0467 | 0.780 |

OLS log residuals sit near zero because OLS minimises exactly this quantity.
Poisson's are shifted negative by about 0.4 in logs, roughly `exp(0.4) = 1.5x`,
because a mean-targeting estimator must over-predict the median of a
right-skewed distribution. **A negative log-residual mean is the expected
signature of a correctly mean-calibrated model here, not evidence of bias.**

Residual SD stays near 1.0 for both. Neither estimator explains more of the
scatter; they place the same scatter differently.

## 3. Error by predicted band (mean observed / mean predicted, target 1.00)

### current

| predicted band | log_ols | n | poisson_qmle | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| under 10k | 1.564 | 225 | 1.984 | 208 |
| 10k to 25k | 1.296 | 467 | **0.977** | 313 |
| 25k to 50k | 1.416 | 300 | **0.878** | 274 |
| 50k to 100k | 2.211 | 141 | **0.813** | 208 |
| over 100k | **3.641** | 81 | **1.125** | 211 |

### pre2022

| predicted band | log_ols | poisson_qmle |
|---|---|---|
| under 10k | 2.338 | 2.707 |
| 10k to 25k | 1.253 | **0.976** |
| 25k to 50k | 1.553 | **0.886** |
| 50k to 100k | 2.025 | **0.900** |
| over 100k | 3.065 | **0.932** |

OLS under-predicts in **every** band and gets monotonically worse with size,
reaching **3.6x** on the largest. Poisson lands four of five bands within
[0.81, 1.13].

Both miss the smallest band, and Poisson misses it by more. That band is
floor-censored: the frame is truncated at `MIN_ANNUAL_PAX = 4,000`, so observed
values there cannot go below the floor while predictions can. This is the defect
Phase 6B targets and neither estimator can fix it.

## 4. Calibration curve, `current`, by predicted decile

Mean observed over mean predicted. Target 1.0 on every row.

| decile | mean_pred | log_ols ratio | poisson ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4.2k to 5.0k | 2.2 | 2.6 |
| 1 | 8.9k to 9.3k | 1.2 | 1.5 |
| 2 | 12k to 14k | 1.6 | 1.2 |
| 3 | 15k to 19k | 1.0 | **0.8** |
| 4 | 19k to 26k | 1.2 | **0.9** |
| 5 | 24k to 36k | 1.4 | **0.9** |
| 6 | 31k to 49k | 1.3 | **0.8** |
| 7 | 40k to 72k | 1.7 | **0.8** |
| 8 | 59k to 122k | 2.0 | **1.0** |
| 9 | 146k to 434k | **3.4** | **1.1** |

OLS is never within 20% of calibrated on any decile above the third and is off
by **3.4x** on the top decile. Poisson holds deciles 3 through 9 inside
[0.8, 1.1]. This is the single clearest exhibit in the comparison.

## 5. Downstream impact: does any of it change a decision?

Counterfactual run through the real pipeline with
`NETWORK_LAB_GRAVITY_ESTIMATOR=poisson_qmle`, changing **only** the demand
estimator. Baseline artifacts restored afterwards.

### Verdict stability

| study | baseline | poisson | changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| westjet_yyc | 0 / 0 / 76 | 0 / 0 / 76 | **0** |
| alaska_sea | 0 / 0 / 45 | 0 / 0 / 45 | **0** |
| porter_yyz | 1 / 1 / 77 | 1 / 1 / 77 | **0** |

**Zero of 200 markets change verdict.**

### Ranking stability

| study | Spearman, demand | Spearman, margin |
|---|---|---|
| westjet_yyc | 0.8816 | 0.9448 |
| alaska_sea | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| porter_yyz | 0.9975 | 0.9996 |

Backtest percentile Spearman **0.9878**; median percentile operating
0.891 to 0.878, ceased 0.859 to 0.859. The null separation result is unchanged.

### Why nothing moves: the transfer factor absorbs it by construction

This is the most important finding in Phase 6A and it is structural, not
numerical.

The transfer factor is estimated as `observed_2018 / gravity_pred`. Poisson
raises `gravity_pred`, so the fitted transfer factor falls by almost exactly the
same proportion:

| hub | log_ols | poisson | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| national median | 0.802 | 0.306 | 0.38x |
| YYC | 1.277 | 0.504 | 0.39x |
| YYZ | 0.778 | 0.265 | 0.34x |
| YVR | 0.828 | 0.314 | 0.38x |

Transborder demand is `gravity_pred x transfer`, so the two changes cancel and
median demand moves by **1.00x**. **Any uniform rescaling of the gravity model is
invisible to transborder demand, because the transfer factor is a ratio to that
same model.** Improving gravity's level calibration cannot improve transborder
estimates under the current architecture.

Meanwhile `alaska_sea` is 45 of 45 `observed` DB1B, so gravity never fires there
at all, which is why its Spearman is exactly 1.0000.

### The one genuine downstream gain

`gravity_x_transfer` fires for the first time. A5 recorded it firing zero times.

| study | capped, baseline | capped, poisson | released |
|---|---|---|---|
| westjet_yyc | 52 | 40 | **12** |
| porter_yyz | 21 | 19 | **2** |

14 markets move off the constant cap onto a real per-market estimate. All move
**down**, from -0.0% to -72.5% (Brownsville-Harlingen -72.5%, McAllen -61.1%,
Gulfport-Biloxi -49.2%). The cap was overstating them.

### A genuine regression

Transfer-factor dispersion gets **worse**, and it is a published metric:

| | log_ols | poisson |
|---|---|---|
| median | 0.802 | 0.306 |
| IQR | [0.546, 2.017] | [0.182, 0.829] |
| IQR ratio hi/lo | 3.70 | **4.56** |
| sd of ln(transfer) | 0.915 | **1.130** |

## 6. Reading the evidence

**Poisson is better at the thing it was built to fix.** Aggregate calibration
0.44 to 0.95, RMSE down 23 to 28%, and the calibration curve flat across seven
deciles where OLS is off by up to 3.4x. For a system whose job is to size
markets it has never served, systematic 3.4x under-prediction of the largest
markets is a more serious defect than a 20% worse median APE, because the large
markets are where a launch decision actually gets made.

**Poisson is worse on per-market relative accuracy**, and that is not an
artifact to be explained away: median APE 0.615 to 0.740 means the typical
market's estimate is proportionally further off.

**Neither matters yet**, because the gravity path is almost entirely bypassed:
observed DB1B for US domestic, observed 2018 anchors or the cap for transborder,
and a transfer factor that structurally cancels any level change.

Recommendation and the adoption decision are in
`docs/phase6a_implementation_report.md`.
